newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea sends first mission abroad since defection.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea sends first mission abroad since defection.

text.p: A North Korean delegation has left for a visit to three European nations in what analysts said was the first such mission since travel curbs were imposed over the defection of a senior official.

The official Korean Central Broadcasting, in a report on Wednesday monitored by Tokyo-based Radiopress, said a Foreign Ministry delegation headed by Vice Foreign Minister Kim Chang-ryong left Pyongyang by train on Tuesday bound for Switzerland, Germany and Norway.
The train was likely to take them to Beijing, where they would take onward flights to Europe.

Radiopress analysts said it was the first such trip by a North Korean delegation since Pyongyang clamped down on travel after Hwang Jang-yop, ranked 24th in the Pyongyang hierarchy, sought asylum at South Korea's mission in China on February 12.
Hwang, North Korea's top ideologue, remains in the diplomatic mission awaiting the resumption of talks between South Korea and China to determine his fate.
The talks, which were put on hold after the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping last Wednesday, were expected to resume this week after Deng's funeral on Tuesday.
